name: NY-22
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+4 PVI) plus favorable environment
Mannion's large financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs $187K)
No public polling to refine the estimate
model.rationale: The baseline model points to a Safe D race with an 18-point margin, and prediction markets agree at ~94% Democratic. Mannion's overwhelming cash advantage and first-time opponent justify only a modest trim toward a 16-point margin.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing the Republican challenger competitive would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-22 is a central New York House district with a modest Democratic lean (D+4), where first-term incumbent John Mannion is seeking reelection. The quantitative baseline combines the district lean, a favorable national environment for Democrats, incumbency, and a large money edge into an expected margin of about 18 points, with fundamentals alone suggesting roughly 15.

Mannion has raised about $2.7 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican challenger Kailee Buller has raised under $300,000 with minimal cash remaining and no visible outside spending on either side. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price the Democrat around 94%. With no public polling or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and markets, supporting a Safe D rating with a slightly tempered expected margin.
